newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds extend gains on S&P upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds extend gains on S&P upgrade.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished higher Wednesday, extending gains on news of an upgrade by Standard & Poor's to the country's debt rating to BB from BB-.
Analysts and traders said the news pushed the market higher, particularly as S&P bypassed its normal procedure of first changing the country's outlook.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/8 to 89-3/4, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.40 to 127.10.
But the market's reaction was not marked by a strong upward surge. There was a brief moment of euphoria but that passed, said traders.
The subdued reaction was put down to the fact that players were largely expecting the news, considering the positive statements by S&P when it first announced the review of Argentine debt.
Also, "in the short-term the market will depend on the behaviour of the U.S. long bond yield," said an analyst.
However analysts suggested the upgrade could draw more funds to Argentine assets over time.
Traders added that the release of the key U.S. unemployment report Friday could keep the market on tenterhooks on Thursday.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 6.70 percent from 6.75 percent.
